{{Citation}}
The '''Navy Order of Battle''' referred to the organization, strength and command structure of the formations of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The [[Order of Battle/Legends|Order of Battle]] was under the purview of the Navy's [[Flight Branch]].<ref name="ISB2">[[Imperial Sourcebook (Second Edition)|''Imperial Sourcebook'', Second Edition]]</ref>

The Order of Battle reflected ideal combat formations and unit strengths, not operational realities. Especially at the higher levels, many Navy formations like the [[Systems force|Systems Force]] and the [[Sector Group/Legends|Sector Group]] were understrength throughout the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Warfare1">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

In the aftermath of the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] and [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] death, the Navy Order of Battle broke down completely: the Imperial Navy split into smaller and smaller operational units as ambitious [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]] and [[Admiral/Legends|Admirals]] seized control of parts of the fleet and set themselves up as [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]].<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

==Order of Battle==
===Command===
An individual command, a single [[Starship/Legends|starship]], was the building block of the Imperial Starfleet. Achieving command of a starship, no matter its size, was point of pride in an officer's career. The most iconic commands of the Imperial Navy were the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]], of which nearly 25,000 were built. Despite this, they were not the most common [[Warship/Legends|warship]] in the Navy: that was the [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]] [[IPV-1 System Patrol Craft]], a heavily-armed [[Corvette/Legends|corvette]].<ref name="Warfare1" />

Officers commonly turned down impressive staff promotions in the hopes of receiving a ship command, although serving as a staff officer on a prominent starship, such as a squadron flagship, was often considered a fast track for promotion. Commanding officers of ships, regardless of their [[Rank insignia plaque/Legends|line rank]], always received the positional title of [[Captain/Legends|''Captain'']].<ref name="Warfare1" />

===Line of battle===
The most basic combat formation in the Imperial Navy was the [[line of battle]], or simply a line, and the smallest organizational unit used for [[Space warfare/Legends|space combat]].<ref name="Handbook" /> The Imperial Starfleet shaped four to twenty starships into lines, depending on the type of line. The line was the most amorphous level of organization in the Starfleet. The Imperial Starfleet Order of Battle outlined seven types of lines: [[Attack line|attack]], [[Heavy attack line|heavy attack]], [[Recon line|reconnaissance]], [[Pursuit line|pursuit]], [[Skirmish line|skirmish]], [[Troop line|troop]] and [[Torpedo line|torpedo]].

Attack and heavy attack lines aggressively engaged enemy starships in combat. Attack lines were composed of three [[Heavy cruiser/Legends|heavy cruisers]], or six to eight [[Cruiser/Legends|light cruisers]], while heavy attack lines were composed of four to eight medium or heavy cruisers, possibly including a [[Victory-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyer]]. If an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer was present to provide direct firepower, attack lines would harry the opponent's flanks.<ref name="Handbook" />

Reconnaissance lines of two to four light cruisers equipped with surveillance gear gathered intelligence of the disposition of enemy forces, and did not engage in direct combat.<ref name="Handbook" />

Pursuit lines of four to ten fast light cruisers or [[Frigate/Legends|frigates]] chased and trapped retreating enemies.<ref name="Handbook" />

Skirmish lines of four to twenty [[Corvette/Legends|corvettes]] or similar small vessels harassed capital starships and engaged enemy pickets, frigates and [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]], providing direct support for [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighters]].<ref name="Handbook" /> Skirmish lines of IPV-1 Patrol Craft were deployed everywhere the Empire wished to maintain a military presence.<ref name="Warfare1" />

A troop line consisted of two [[Evakmar]]-[[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]] [[Evakmar-KDY transport|Corps Transport]] vessels, two escort vessels, and frequently two [[Strike-class medium cruiser|''Strike''-class medium cruisers]]. Its function was the deployment of [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] units.<ref name="Handbook" />

A [[torpedo line]] consisted of up to two [[Torpedo Sphere/Legends|Torpedo Spheres]], used to penetrate [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shields]].<ref name="Handbook" />

In addition to the seven types of lines, the Imperial Navy considered an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer a line in itself. While an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer may have been able to act as an attack line and its complement of starfighters as a skirmish line, the decision to give commanders the option to field a ship equivalent to a heavy cruiser as a line unto itself was more political than tactical. After a naval staff study suggested a Star Destroyer was the field equivalent of the smallest of naval squadrons, the Admiralty decided that, as there were more lines than squadrons, designating the Star Destroyer as a line unit would get them more Star Destroyers. The Admiralty's thinking prevailed.

Lines of battle were commanded by [[Captain of the Line/Legends|Senior Captains]], who received the positional title of ''[[Captain of the Line/Legends|Captain of the Line]]''.<ref name="Warfare1" />

===Squadron===
[[File:Imperial_Starfleet.jpg|thumb|right|''Imperial''-class [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] and [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighters]] at the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].]]
A [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]] was the smallest independent operating unit in the Imperial Navy. Composed of several lines, a squadron ranged from 14 to 60 ships, depending upon the composition of the lines in the squadron. A squadron was the largest concentration of ships normally assigned to a single system. The [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] had designated units of identical configuration as fleets, which had been the total naval presence in a sector. Thus, the subordination and vast growth in numbers of squadrons was a useful measure of the growth of the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] after the establishment of Emperor [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[New Order/Legends|New Order]].

Similar to lines, the Imperial Navy's Order of Battle designated four types of squadrons: [[Light squadron|light]], [[Heavy squadron|heavy]], [[Battle squadron|battle]], and [[Bombard squadron|bombard]].

Light squadrons patrolled areas known to be safe with a skirmish line and a reconnaissance line,<ref name="Handbook" /> and optionally two attack lines.

Heavy squadrons engaged planetary systems that possessed known enemy presences with two heavy attack lines. In situations where pinpointing the enemy's position was required, heavy squadrons may be reinforced with an attack line and a reconnaissance line. During aggressive operations against the enemy, or those where the enemy was known to be defending a fixed asset the heavy squadron may consist of three heavy attack lines and a skirmish line.<ref name="Handbook" /> It was common to assign [[Victory I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyers]] to the latter type of heavy squadron.

Battle squadrons contained an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer, supported by at least three lines - two attack lines and one pursuit line - for an average of 18 ships. In practice, [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] were normally accompanied by just two or three escorts, if any: the ''Imperial''-class was designed to operate without support, and its [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] was too fast for any escorts except for the speediest light cruisers. The battle squadron was used for offensive operations against a known enemy, and the mere arrival of an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer was often enough to put down a planetary revolt or scare off an armed space-threat.<ref name="Handbook" />

Bombard squadrons subjugated worlds in open rebellion that had developed planetary defenses including multilayered planetary shields and large planetary guns with a skirmish line, a pursuit line, and up to four Torpedo Spheres. In practice, however, such squadrons usually only contained one Torpedo Sphere.<ref name="Handbook" />

The squadron's flag officer was officially of [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]] rank, though he usually received the positional title of [[Commander/Legends|''Commander'']].<ref name="Warfare1" />

====Training Squadrons====
Like other navies in the past, the Imperial Navy utilized various [[training squadron]]s, which were commanded by cadets who had passed through initial pilot training. [[Bantha Squad]] and the [[Unidentified training squadron|training squadron]] on ''Victorious'' were a few of these training squadrons.

====Notable squadrons====
[[File:Executordeathsquad.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Death Squadron, lead by the ''Executor'']]
The Imperial Navy had several squadrons at its disposal. The [[123rd Nightstalker Group]], under the command of [[Cronal|Blackhole]], was comprised wholly of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighters]] and participated in various combat operations during the Galactic Civil War. In addition, the [[128th TIE Interceptor Squadron]] was an elite TIE/IN interceptor squadron, formerly led by [[Kasan Moor/Legends|Kasan Moor]] until her defection to the Rebel Alliance. Other TIE/IN interceptor squadrons included the [[133rd Imperial Fighter Group]] under [[Xandel Carivus]] and the [[181st Imperial Fighter Wing/Legends|181st Imperial Fighter Wing]], later renamed the 181st Imperial Fighter Group led by Soontir Fel, which became elite under his command. The 181st Imperial Fighter Wing had several subsections, including the [[2/181st]] and [[Alpha Squadron (TIE/IN interceptor)/Legends|Alpha Squadron]]. The [[37th Imperial Fighter Wing]] was also involved in the [[Battle of Saloch]], where it was composed of at least 6 squadrons, including the [[6/37th]]. Zsinj once had the 181st Imperial Fighter Group [[Zsinj's impostor 181st Imperial Fighter Group|impersonated]]. The [[Black Eight Squadron]] was an elite TIE/LN and [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa bomber]] squadron, of which its most notable member was [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]], one of the leaders of the Rebel Alliance. It eventually was reorganized by 1 ABY. [[Avenger Squadron/Legends|Avenger Squadron]] was another notable squadron, being composed almost entirely of TIE Avengers and was assigned to the Task Force Vengeance. [[Storm Squadron/Legends|Storm Squadron]] likewise was composed entirely of TIE Advanced X1s.

[[Black Squadron (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Black Squadron]] was a TIE fighter squadron personally commanded by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], although most of the squadron was wiped out during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. It was well known enough that several Imperial Starfighter Squadrons derived their names from it, a notable example being [[Onyx Squadron/Legends|Onyx Squadron]].

Although technically a fleet, [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]] was one of the most notable squadrons, being under the direct command of Vader. It was composed of several warships, including the ''Executor'', the first in the ''Executor''-line of Star Dreadnoughts, which acted as its flagship. It also was composed of several other squadrons under its wing, including the 128th TIE Interceptor Squadron, the TIE/LN starfighter [[Obsidian Squadron/Legends|Obsidian Squadron]], and the TIE/sa bomber [[Scimitar Squadron (Imperial)/Legends|Scimitar Squadron]].

Although not actually part of the Imperial Navy, the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] sometimes acted as a starfighter squadron for the Imperial Navy. In addition, [[Black Wing Squadron]] was also developed based on the Rebel Alliance/New Republic starfighter squadron [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]], with the intention of having them fight it.

[[File:Youngster-XWM.png|thumb|right|250px|Black Eight Squadron]]
Because of the importance of the Death Star II's construction as well as the Battle of Endor, several squadrons had been reassigned to defend the battlestation, including Death Squadron, [[Scythe Squadron/Legends|Scythe Squadron]] (which had originally been assigned to the Anoat system), Onyx Squadron (which had utilized TIE Defenders for the occasion) and the 181st Imperial Fighter Wing.

There were also some who were assigned to defend the Emperor, such as the [[The Emperor's Sword|Emperor's Sword]] and [[Emperor's Shield]].

During the early years of the Galactic Empire, the [[77th Air Wing]] was utilized during the Western Reaches Operation, which had been composed of a squadron called [[Sword Squadron (Imperial)|Sword Squadron]], made up of 3 flights, [[Dagger Flight]], [[Blade Flight]], and [[Scimitar Flight]]. Another squadron was the [[12th Squadron]].

Other squadrons included the [[276th Imperial TIE Bomber Group]], [[323rd Imperial TIE Bomber Group]], [[Alpha Squadron]], [[Bantha Squad]], [[Beta Squadron/Legends|Beta Squadron]], [[Broadaxe Squadron]], [[Cloak Force]], [[Crimson Squadron (Galactic Empire)|Crimson Squadron]], [[Delta Squadron (TIE/D)/Legends|Delta Squadron]], [[Dark Side Squadron]], [[Dark Squadron/Legends|Dark Squadron]], [[Durkii Squadron]], [[Eagle Squadron]], [[Ebon Squadron]], [[Elite Squadron]], [[Eta Squadron]], [[Gamma Squadron/Legends|Gamma Squadron]], the [[Garqi Eagles]], [[GoldWing Squadron]], [[Hammer Squadron (Galactic Empire)|Hammer Squadron]], [[Interloper Squadron]], [[Iota Squadron (TIE starfighters)|Iota Squadron]], [[Mu Squadron]], [[Nu Squadron (TIE/LN)|Nu Squadron]], [[Raven Squadron]], [[Reaver Squadron]], [[Red Squadron (Imperial)|Red Squadron]], [[Red Star Squadron]], [[Requiem Squadron]], [[Saber Squadron (Imperial)/Legends|Saber Squadron]], [[Scimitar assault wing]], [[Shadow Squadron (Galactic Empire)|Shadow Squadron]], the [[Shadow Squadron (TIE Defender)|TIE Defender squadron]] of the same name, [[Shadow wing]], [[Shrike Squadron (Mandalore)|Shrike Squadron]] on Mandalore, [[Shrike Squadron (Saffalore)|Shrike Squadron]] on Saffalore, [[Sigma Squadron (TIE/ph Phantom)|Sigma Squadron]], [[SilverWing Squadron]], [[Solaest Fleet Long Range Patrol Wing]], [[Spear Squadron]], [[Specter Squadron (Imperial)|Specter Squadron]], [[Stranger Squadron]], [[Sunspot Squadron]], [[Talon Squadron (Galactic Empire)|Talon Squadron]], [[Tempest Squadron/Legends|Tempest Squadron]], [[Theta Squadron (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Theta Squadron]], the TIE/sa bomber squadron of [[Theta Squadron (TIE/sa)|the same name]], [[Twilight Squadron (Imperial)|Twilight Squadron]], [[Veerpal Squadron]], the [[302nd Flight Wing]], and [[Zeta Squadron (TIE Bomber)|Zeta Squadron]].

Some squadrons, such as [[Black Epsilon]], were deployed for covert operations that were either too small or too sensitive for the Navy itself to get involved.

Several squadrons were also created for the Imperial Navy's successors in the Fel Empire and Krayt's Sith Empire, such as the [[1st Imperial Center Core Defense Squadron]], and [[Red Squadron (Sith Empire)|Red Squadron]].

===Systems force===
[[File:ImperialHangar-SWR.png|thumb|left|250px|A typical [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] hangar.]]
A systems force combined several squadrons, typically totalling ninety ships, and was responsible for Imperial Starfleet actions across multiple star systems.<ref name="Handbook" /> In practice, however, despite their nominal strength, most systems forces contained only a single squadron.<ref name="Warfare1" /> Perhaps because of this, rather than outline specific formations of system forces, the Imperial Starfleet Order of Battle lent flexibility to Commodores to pool the whole of their naval resources and shape them as necessary missions required. However, in general, the systems force had at least six possible pooling situations.

[[Force superiority]] pooled at least three battle squadrons and a light squadron.<ref name="Handbook" /> With a minimum of three ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers and nearly 90 other starships, force superiority's mission was to achieve space superiority in a given system, defined as; "the complete absence of hostile craft within the orbital space of controlled worlds, and no chronic enemy ship activity within the entire system." Should an enemy be too powerful for force superiority to successfully destroy, the Commodore had the option of swapping out the light squadron for a fourth battle squadron, thus gaining enough force to ensure complete domination of a target area.

[[Force escort]] protected crucial commercial shipments, economically essential space installations or facilities, and hunted down harassing pirates. With at least two heavy squadrons and two light squadrons,<ref name="Handbook" /> force escort was the most flexible of the force pools. Commodores used force escort to run a variety of missions, knowing well that their large starship count and organizational flexibility would allow for their completion. Where force superiority was given the maxim "always send enough", force escort bore the maxim "never send too much". In practice, this meant that force escorts were the Empire's first line of defense, protecting civilian freighters, attacking [[Corsair (Derriphan-class)|''Corsairs''']] hideouts, and serving as guardships at remote outposts. The Empire's early force escorts relied heavily on [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvettes]] and [[Frigate/Legends|frigates]] captured from the [[Trade Defense Force]] in the aftermath of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], but soon came to included cheap new designs from Kuat Drive Yards, including the [[Ton-Falk-class escort carrier|''Ton-Falk''-class escort carrier]] and the [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 ''Nebulon-B'' escort frigate]].<ref name="Warfare1" />

[[Transport force]]s were charged with deploying various troops from other branches of the Imperial Military, including Army troopers and even [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtroopers]], as well as acting as command centers for any ongoing surface operation. As such, they are comprised of at least two troop squadrons, a heavy squadron, and a light squadron.<ref name="Handbook" />

[[System bombard]] was charged with carrying out planetary bombardment missions. It was composed of three bombard squadrons and one light squadron.<ref name="Handbook" />

[[Force technical services]] was charged with transporting mechanical specialists quickly and safely wherever they are needed most. They are composed of eight transports as well as two armed escort frigates.<ref name="Handbook" />

[[Force support]] was tasked with resupplying various Imperial depots, including planet-side depots, across the galaxy, and as such, contained over a hundred container vessels.<ref name="Handbook" /> They generally lacked escort vessels of their own, but were assigned some when going through combat zones.

Systems forces were commanded by [[Admiral/Legends|Admirals]], who were given the positional titles of [[Systems admiral|''Systems Admiral'']] or [[Commodore/Legends|''Commodore'']]. In practice, however, since most systems forces contained just one combat squadron, the Systems Admiral and the Squadron Commander were the same officer.<ref name="Warfare1" />

===Fleet===
[[File:Imperial_Fleet.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Part of the fleet.]]
Where all previous units were generally bound to specific system or set of systems, the Imperial Navy designated a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] as a "sector resource", allowing it to operate on a sector-wide scale. A fleet was the smallest unit transferred between sectors. Comprising multiple systems forces, fleets typically totalled up to four hundred ships. With such a large number of units, there were thousands of potential types of fleet alignments. Common fleet deployment types included [[superiority fleet]]s, [[assault fleet]]s, and [[bombard fleet]]s. Other examples of formations that a fleet might have taken included a [[deepdock fleet]], [[support fleet]], or ordnance fleet.

Superiority fleets maintained space superiority in sectors with "four or fewer worlds confirmed hostile to the New Order, and no more than 16 additional worlds with confirmed significant hostile elements". With six ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers and almost 400 other starships, a superiority fleet was presumed to be a sufficient force for relatively calm sectors.<ref name="Handbook" />

Assault fleets transported huge numbers of Imperial Army and Navy troops to coordinate ground operations, while maintaining space superiority around the targeted systems. With two transport forces and two force escorts, an assault fleet engaged in massive planetary and system-wide ground campaigns.<ref name="Handbook" />

Bombard fleets contained an average of 416 ships, allocated between two system bombards and two force escorts. Bombard fleets were assigned to high-threat, low-value sectors where the Empire had determined the probability of repressing the Rebellion in the sector to be less than even. System bombards were used to annihilate opposition without concern for local infrastructure, when the Empire would rather completely destroy a world than see it fall into Rebel hands.<ref name="Handbook" />

Deepdock fleets had a total of 280 support vessels and one escort force, and are primarily utilized to support two space-based shipyards. The deepdock complexes in question have over a hundred repair bays with hyperdrive engines to ensure that they were easily relocated.<ref name="Handbook" />

Support fleets were considered the most important non-combat formations in the Navy, charged with securing the logistics of the entire Empire. Support fleets had over 500 small vessels, most of them container ships, with the supply burden falling in equal part on [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvettes]] and massive [[Field Secured Container Vessel/Legends|FSCV transports]].<ref name="Warfare1" /> These fleets equip Imperial military forces with weapons, ammunition, equipment, supplies, and consumables.<ref name="Handbook" />

Fleets were commanded by [[Admiral/Legends|admirals]] given the positional title of [[Fleet Admiral/Legends|''Fleet Admiral'']]. Where [[Sector Group/Legends|Sector Groups]] were not big enough to justify splitting them into separate fleets, this usually made the Fleet Admiral the senior professional officer in the sector.<ref name="Warfare1" />

====Notable fleets====
Fleets within the Imperial Navy include the [[15th Deep Core Reserve Fleet/Legends|15th Deep Core Reserve Fleet]]; the [[27th Denarian Fleet]]; [[Admiral Kohrin's second fleet]]; [[Banjeer's fleet]]; the [[Black Fleet]]; the Byss Defense Fleet; the [[Centrality Navy]]; the [[Chandrila Defense Fleet]]; the [[Charis Fleet]]; the [[Coruscant Defense Fleet/Legends|Coruscant Defense Fleet]]; [[Crimson Command]]; Death Squadron; [[Digit Squadron]]; [[Imperial Replenishment Fleet DK-209/Legends|Imperial Replenishment Fleet DK-209]]; the [[First Naval Fleet]]; the [[Gandle Ott system defense force]]; the [[Grand Imperial Navy]]; the [[Ground Pounders]]; the [[Hammer Group]]; the [[Imperial Fourth Attack Squadron]]; the [[Imperial Outer Rim Territories Patrol Fleet]]; the [[Inner fleet]]; [[Lumiya's fleet]]; the [[Maw fleet]]; the [[Outer Rim Imperial Fleet]]; [[Qeimet fleet]]; the [[Secret armada]]; the [[Shadow Hand Fleet]]; the [[Swift Wing]]; [[Task Force Vengeance/Legends|Task Force Vengeance]]; [[Task Force Whirlwind]]; the [[Third Ado Superiority Fleet]]; [[Thrawn's fleet (Galactic Empire)|Thrawn's fleet]]; the [[Torize planetary defense force]]; the [[Vengeance Battle Group]]; and the [[Western Reaches Superiority Force]]. In addition, there was also one Unidentified Imperial fleet and one [[Unidentified Imperial task force|task force]].

===Sector group===
{{Quote|The Empire's standard Sector Group strength was only twenty-four Star Destroyers. They were able to exercise control over an entire system with a single ''Imperial''-class ship. They were able to overwhelm anything up to a Class Four planetary defense with one-third of a Sector Group.|[[Etahn A'baht]].|<ref name="BeforeStorm">''[[Before the Storm]]''</ref>}}
A [[Sector Group/Legends|Sector Group]] was the sum total of Naval strength which the Empire expected to commit to a normal sector. A sector group could be expected to contain at least 2,400 ships in multiple fleets, 24 of which were Star Destroyers (''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers were the norm, but some groups contained older model Star Destroyers), and another 1,600 combat starships.

The Sector Group level of command came about somewhat by accident: the Moffs of the Empire's sectors, installed under the [[Sector Governance Decree/Legends|Sector Governance Decree]] in the final days of the Republic, complained that the Imperial Navy's force requirements in quelling [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|Separatist holdouts]] routinely robbed their sectors of resources without sufficient consideration for local security needs. Under the Sector Governance Decree, the Moffs held the power of the old [[Governor-General/Legends|Governor-Generals]] to raise forces and began raising their own local [[Militia/Legends|militias]]. Alarmed by the prospect of local military forces not loyal to [[Coruscant/Legends|Imperial Center]], the [[Admiralty (Imperial)/Legends|Admiralty]] stepped in and created Sector Groups, local forces directly controlled by the Moffs but carefully scrutinised by Coruscant.<ref name="Warfare1" />

The Sector Groups were largely drawn from the [[Planetary Security Forces]], [[Imperialization/Legends|nationalized]] after the [[Declaration of a New Order]], with its combat forces split between [[force superiority]] and [[force escort]], and separate fleet commands for [[Assault fleet|troop transport]], [[Bombard fleet|bombardment]], [[Deepdock fleet|deepdock]] and [[support fleet]]s. In practice, Sector Groups were rarely at their full establishment strength, sometimes lacking enough discrete forces to justify dividing the group into separate superiority and escort fleets.<ref name="Warfare1" />

The commander of a Sector Group received the title of ''[[High Admiral]]'', but this was often a ceremonial post granted to the [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] who governed the sector.<ref name="Warfare1" /> In sectors that were involved in constant and severe naval actions, however, the [[High Admiral]] was a separate position from the Moff.

The sector groups included [[Azure Shield]], assigned alongside the 1st Sector Army, Azure Hammer Command, to the [[Azure sector/Legends|Azure sector]] of the [[Imperial Center Oversector]]; the [[Baxel sector fleet]], assigned to the [[Baxel sector/Legends|Baxel sector]]; the [[Brak Sector Fleet]], assigned to the [[Brak sector/Legends|Brak sector]]; the [[Braxant Sector Fleet]], a fleet composed of 13 ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers assigned to the [[Braxant sector/Legends|Braxant sector]] that included the ''Obliterator'', ''Ironhand'', ''Relentless'', and the ''Tyrannic''; the [[Ferrouz's sector fleet|Candoras Sector Fleet]], composed of four ''Dreadnought''-class heavy cruisers and other smaller ships assigned to the [[Candoras sector/Legends|Candoras sector]]; the [[Coruscant Sector Fleet]], assigned to Coruscant due to it being a sector in itself; the [[Elrood Sector Fleet]], assigned to the [[Elrood sector/Legends|Elrood sector]] composed of the ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers ''Stalker'' and ''Thunderflare'', the ''Bayonet''-class light cruiser ''Rintonne's Flame'', and smaller vessels, including 12 system patrol craft, custom vessels, Skipray Blastboats, and various TIE fighters; the [[Kathol Sector Imperial Fleet]], assigned to the [[Kathol sector/Legends|Kathol sector]]; the [[Kuati Sector Forces]], assigned to the defense of Kuat; the [[Oplovis Sector Fleet]], assigned to the [[Oplovis sector/Legends|Oplovis sector]]; the [[Tapani Defense Force]], assigned to the [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]]; the [[Tierfon Sector Fleet]], assigned to the [[Sumitra sector/Legends|Tierfon sector]]; and the [[Trax Sector Group]], assigned to the [[Trax sector/Legends|Trax sector]].

===Regional, oversector and strategic command===
[[File:PlanetaryBombardment-SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|left|220px|A fleet consisting of ''Executor''-class Dreadnoughts, ''Imperial''-class Destroyers and Nebulon-B frigates conduct an [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|orbital bombardment]].]]
Although the Sector Group was the highest strength in the standard Order of Battle, there were also higher unofficial levels known as regional groups and [[Oversector/Legends|Oversector]] groups, formed by assembled by merging sector groups together.<ref name="Handbook" /> Regional, [[Oversector/Legends|oversector]] and strategic military commands came in a variety of mixed<ref name="SW60">[[Star Wars (1977) 60|''Star Wars'' (1977) 60]]</ref> and homogeneous<ref name="GSOTE">''[[Goroth: Slave of the Empire]]''</ref> forces. These formations, however, are not officially part of the standard Order of Battle.<ref name="Handbook" />

[[Sixth Negative Regions|Black Sword Command]] was a regional command that defended the Core regions from threats emanating from the galactic rim. It had three Super Star Destroyers as part of its fleet assets.<ref name="BFC">''[[The Black Fleet Crisis]]''</ref> [[First Army|Azure Hammer Command]], based out of [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]], defended [[Imperial Center Oversector|Sector Zero]] and consisted of 57 capital ships, led by the Super Star Destroyer ''[[Whelm]]''.<ref name="CATCW">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]''</ref> Likewise, [[Tenth Army|Crimson Dagger Command]], also based out of [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]], defended the [[Quelii Oversector]], and was instrumental in the [[Ciutric Offensive]] during the [[Reconquest of the Rim]] in the early stages of the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]]. [[Twelfth Army/Legends|Cerulean Spear Command]], likewise, was charged with the defense of the [[Maldrood Oversector/Legends|Maldrood Oversector]], and was instrumental in the [[Sy Myrthian Insurrection]] during that same time period.<ref name="Warfare1" /> Additionally, a full ten percent of the entire Imperial Navy was kept in reserve in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], so as to be able to quickly respond to threats throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="SWSB">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref> In the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], a [[Outer Rim Imperial Fleet|fleet]] with at least 19 ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers and three [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|Immobilizer 418 cruisers]], the latter supplied by [[Imperial Drydock IV]], was also kept.<ref name="X-wing">[[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]</ref>

Roving fleets aimed at specific tasks were fielded at several points in Imperial history. Notable units included [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]]<ref name="ISB">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref><ref name="RASB">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref> and [[Scourge Squadron]],<ref name="TPA">{{JournalCite|3|The Pentastar Alignment}}</ref> which hunted for Rebel bases in the Outer Rim. There was also the [[Vengeance Battle Group]], used by the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] to search for the [[Valley of the Jedi]],<ref name="DF:JK">''[[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight]]''</ref> and the [[secret armada]] assembled by [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Mils Giel]], for the purpose of transporting a vital biological device from the Outer Rim to Imperial Center.<ref name="SW60" />

At least one [[Star Destroyer task force]] was used to punish Imperial sectors that threatened to undermine Imperial rule, as when the [[Moff (Trans-Nebular sector)|Moff]] of the [[Trans-Nebular sector/Legends|Trans-Nebular sector]] established himself as the de facto warlord and was engaged by a fleet of Star Destroyers. This force was large enough to leave behind vessels that would form the core of a new sector fleet, before moving on to other trouble spots.<ref name="GSOTE" /> There was also a [[Byss Defense Fleet|fleet]] stationed near [[Byss/Legends|Byss]], that was formed since the start of the Galactic Empire. The Emperor himself also possessed a [[Emperor's fleet|personal fleet]] that he has command over, utilizing it in situations important enough to require him to participate in person.

==Starfighter Corps organization==
{{Main|Starfighter Corps (Galactic Empire)/Legends}}
[[File:EndorEntrapment-TCGSBI.png|thumb|right|250px|An array of Imperial starfighters at the Battle of Endor]]
The [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Fighters]] of the Imperial Navy's [[Starfighter Corps (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Starfighter Corps]] were organized as follows:

*'''[[Flight/Legends|Element]]''': 2 starfighters, consisting of a leader and a [[Wingmate/Legends|wingmate]].
*'''[[Flight group/Legends|Flight]]''': 4 starfighters in 2 elements.
*'''[[Squadron/Legends|Squadron]]''': 12 starfighters in 3 flights.
*'''[[Fighter wing/Legends|Wing]]''': 72 starfighters in 2 groups, typical complement of an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]]

The typical formation of an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer's wing was four [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighter]] squadrons (one squadron was often equipped to be a reconnaissance squadron with [[TIE/rc starfighter]]s), one squadron of [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE Bombers]] (lower priority ships had to make do with older [[TIE/gt starfighter|TIE/gt fighter-bombers]]), and one squadron of [[TIE/br boarding shuttle|TIE Boarding Craft]]. Often one or two flights in a fighter squadron were [[TIE/fc starfighter|TIE/FC fire control craft]]. Sometimes one of the fighter squadrons was used for training purposes. By the Battle of Endor, one squadron had been swapped out in favor of a squadron of TIE Interceptors.<ref name="Vehicles">''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> During typical operations, two TIE squadrons provided screening for their Star Destroyer and any escort vessels, two conducted forward recon, and two were held in reserve.<ref name="Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-10-the-rise-of-the-empire|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 10: The Rise of the Empire}} {{1stID|Starfighter Corps}}</ref>

TIE Fighters assigned to ground operations were Navy vessels, but their pilots reported to an [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] garrison commander, organized into [[ground support wing]]s.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> The Navy's insistence on retaining control of all starfighters meant that ground support wings were smaller than those assigned to Star Destroyers, and consisted of forty TIEs in ten flights of four fighters each. Three flights were TIE Bombers, six were sorted into two [[Squadron/Legends|squadrons]] of TIE Fighters, and a single flight of [[TIE/fc starfighter|TIE/FC fire control craft]].<ref name="ISB" />
